approval_required_for: Authorization to implement and deploy planned_tool.remote_vcs_termination_disambiguation and planned_checker.termination_provenance_completeness in the framework remote VCS runner/evidence-analyzer path before relying on a fresh replay.

A bounded human decision only if cited live sample-project/Vivado evidence remains ambiguous about the exact board top, wrapper/source identity, export context, or authorized simulator executable; no target may be guessed.

consumes: current user-supplied board wrapper and complete source-hash manifest
current Vivado export facts and export contexts
current board simulation identity and VCS compile-plan records
executable_actions.on_failure: Keep functional simulation and all downstream board gates blocked. If live evidence cannot uniquely bind the exact board top, wrapper/source hashes, Vivado-export context, command executable, or tool authority, request bounded approval with the competing cited artifacts; do not guess a target name, synthesize a substitute wrapper, or patch RTL.
executable_actions.rationale: The direct current failure is stale or incomplete binding between the board-simulation identity, exact user-supplied sample-project wrapper/source hashes, Vivado export facts, ordered VCS commands, and simulator executable authorization. Reconstruct these metadata bindings from live cited artifacts without modifying the wrapper, testbench semantic contract, checkpoint, stimulus, numeric policy, or DUT RTL.

consumes: current wall-time and simulation-cycle budget configuration
executable_actions.on_failure: Block VCS replay and retain all active SACG barriers. Do not infer an RTL, loader, AXI, DDR, deadlock, or analyzer defect from absent reports, and do not weaken the simulator timeout, numeric policy, or acceptance criteria.
executable_actions.rationale: The framework remote VCS runner and evidence analyzer lack the capability needed to distinguish simulator/DUT failure from external termination or timeout. This is a verification-capability implementation gap, not hardware correctness evidence, and must be resolved before modifying board RTL, testbench behavior, or report schemas in response to missing completion reports.

consumes: current immutable target checkpoint and complete tensor catalog
current numeric comparison policy and resolved tolerances
current generated semantic testbench hashes and board harness manifest
executable_actions.on_failure: Classify failure as a checker/golden-reference, loader, or harness-contract repair. Preserve checkpoint, stimulus, target reference, tolerance, testbench hashes, and wrapper hashes; never generate expected outputs randomly or from RTL output, sample weights as complete coverage, or add embedding/tokenization/model-tail requirements to the DUT.
executable_actions.rationale: Before any board functional claim, confirm that the exact wrapper-bound harness uses complete Transformer-block checkpoint tensors, immutable deterministic/real stimulus, independent target-model expected outputs, immutable generated testbench hashes, frozen numeric comparison policy, and complete bound-loader consumption requirements. This reuses lower-layer certificates without reopening their modules and excludes model-tail work from the DUT scope.

consumes: current exact board-wrapper and simulation-source hashes
executable_actions.on_failure: If termination is external, killed, timed out, or otherwise unclassified, return to repair.enable_remote_vcs_termination_provenance and make no hardware claim. If normal completion reports a real failure, localize the earliest current board boundary and repair only the implicated wrapper/harness/integration slice. Do not reopen a lower layer unless the fresh trace directly contradicts a named certificate invariant with hash-bound core-start, ingress, egress, causal-boundary, and current-certificate evidence.
executable_actions.rationale: After exact identity binding, semantic-contract validation, and termination-provenance support are available, obtain fresh current-layer evidence. The replay must use the exact board wrapper and authorized VCS plan and must capture direct lifecycle/core-start, ingress, egress, AXI/DDR progress, output/lifecycle frontier, raw terminal output, and termination classification before any repair is selected.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep board promotion blocked and emit a fresh current-layer causal slice for the earliest failed gate. A frontier stall is localization evidence only; do not treat independent AXI/prefetch progress as output progress or select an RTL root cause without the fresh trace. A lower-kernel backtrack remains prohibited absent the required direct named contradiction.
executable_actions.rationale: A normally completed replay with valid identity and semantic evidence is the prerequisite for the remaining current board-layer gates. Execute them in dependency order to establish real functional, ordering, liveness, AXI protocol, DDR image, and semantic-evidence status; this is required before any promotion and is not a lower-layer rerun.

consumes: current scoped SACG open retry requests
executable_actions.on_failure: Retain active barriers and open retries, treat all rejected artifacts as planning/debug evidence only, and return to the earliest failed current-layer action. Do not clear barriers, consume the candidate as validated downstream input, or promote to backend/board runtime.
produces: updated SACG retry/barrier status linked to fresh Stage7 evidence
promotion-eligibility decision or retained current-layer repair request
executable_actions.rationale: Active barriers and retry_request.0136, retry_request.0140, retry_request.0141, retry_request.0142, retry_request.0143, and retry_request.0144 must remain operational until a fresh Stage7 candidate has passed all current board-layer gates. Reconciliation must distinguish rejected historical artifacts from the new candidate and may not promote merely because a repair plan exists.

observations: real_tool.case_axi_ddr_interface failed because simulation.source_identity_sha256, Vivado-export compile authority, ordered-command authority references, and simulator executable authorization do not bind the current exact sample-project identity. This is a current board-integration verification-contract failure, not RTL failure evidence.

functional_sim=fail is dependency-derived: real_tool.case_vcs_functional_sim was not run because case_axi_ddr_interface is not pass. Therefore the missing board semantic evidence and other downstream reports are evidence gaps/cascades, not independent proof of loader, AXI, DDR, pipeline, numeric, or DUT defects.

The current debug closure has no failed boundary, root candidate module, or localized failing transaction and classifies the state as a verification_capability_gap. Its historical VCS diagnosis is explicitly unbound to current sources and must not be used as root-cause evidence.

Prior current-scope repair feedback additionally reports a completed VCS compile followed by remote_tool_failure without raw terminal log, signal, timeout/kill, wall-time, or simulation-cycle termination provenance. Missing dynamic reports from that run cannot justify testbench, analyzer, wrapper, or RTL modification until remote termination is classified.

Hash-validated operator-leaf and connected single-transformer-layer certificates remain reusable. The current trace does not contradict a named lower-layer invariant; specifically, it does not justify reopening the elastic variable-latency kernel, whose certified semantics require boundary order and cross-token overlap rather than strict same-cycle stage completion.

sacg_memory_truth is authoritative for this scope and reports 15 active contamination barriers and six open retry requests, including retry_request.0143 and retry_request.0144 for the current case_axi_ddr_interface/functional_sim failure. There are no scoped open backtrack requests. Rejected Stage7/Stage8 artifacts remain planning/debug evidence only until a fresh Stage7 pass is recorded.
The conditional design-team route returned no_split. It supplies no specialist evidence that can replace the failed deterministic checker or authorize a hardware repair.
proposed_actions: Rebind the board simulation identity and canonical VCS compile plan to the exact current sample-project wrapper, source hashes, real Vivado export contexts, and authorized simulator executable; do not change board RTL or guess integration targets.
Implement or authorize the missing framework remote-VCS termination-provenance capture/checker before relying on another VCS replay.

Audit the immutable board semantic replay contract for target-model reference, Transformer-block weight coverage, loader consumption, input provenance, testbench hashes, and frozen numeric policy without regenerating lower-layer evidence or expected outputs from DUT data.
Run one fresh current-layer VCS boundary replay with full termination provenance and causal monitors. Localize only an actual, earliest current-layer violation.
Only after a normally completed semantic replay passes, execute the dependency-ordered remaining board verification gates and then reconcile SACG retry/trust records from the fresh Stage7 result.
risks: Board identity risk: a stale or guessed top, wrapper, Vivado export context, simulator executable, or command order would invalidate board results even if compilation succeeds. The exact user-supplied wrapper and source hashes must be cited rather than substituted.

Remote-runtime risk: without normal-completion versus simulator-fatal versus external-termination/timeout classification, absent completion reports cannot be attributed to RTL liveness, output-frontier, AXI, DDR, loader, or analyzer behavior.

Model, data, and numeric risk: a board functional pass requires a complete Transformer-block tensor catalog, bound loader/harness proof that every required block weight was consumed, deterministic/real input provenance, target-model expected outputs for the same immutable checkpoint and input, and immutable resolved comparison tolerances. Embedding/tokenization, final norm, LM head/logits, and sampling remain outside the DUT golden and weight-coverage scope.

Order, memory, and runtime risk: independent AXI/prefetch progress is not output/lifecycle-frontier progress. Any later frontier stall must be localized from current core-start, ingress, egress, causal-boundary, and completion evidence before selecting a wrapper or kernel root cause.

Lower-layer regression risk: an output/frontier symptom alone cannot reopen the certified connected kernel. Revalidation requires a fresh hash-bound trace directly contradicting a named lower-layer invariant with core start, ingress, egress, causal-boundary, and current-certificate evidence.

SACG trust risk: active contamination barriers and open retry requests block downstream consumption and promotion; they must be reconciled only from a fresh passing Stage7 candidate, not by reusing or editing rejected outputs.

constraints: exact user-supplied board-wrapper and Vivado-export binding
no lower-layer reopen without a current named contradictory trace
edges: immutable board semantic replay contract -> fresh VCS replay -> board dynamic gate DAG -> case_board_semantic_evidence
fresh current-layer trace -> current-layer wrapper/harness localization
fresh trace with named hash-bound lower-layer contradiction -> targeted lower-layer backtrack only
fresh complete Stage7 pass -> SACG retry/barrier reconciliation -> promotion eligibility
